record.original_question: For a real polynomial system f_1(x,y)=f_2(x,y)=0, where f_i has m_i monomials, is (2m_1 - 1)(2m_2 - 1) the maximum possible number of simple real solutions?

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Is (2m1 - 1)(2m2 - 1) the maximum number of simple solutions of a real polynomial system f1(x, y) = f2(x, y) = 0, where mi is the number of monomials of each fi?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f_1(x,y), f_2(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}[x,y]$ be two real polynomials in two variables. For $i=1,2$, let $m_i$ denote the number of (distinct) monomials appearing with nonzero coefficient in $f_i$. A solution $(x_0,y_0)$ of the system $f_1(x,y)=f_2(x,y)=0$ in $(\mathbb{R}^*)^2$ (i.e., with $x_0 y_0 \neq 0$) is called simple if the Jacobian of $(f_1,f_2)$ at $(x_0,y_0)$ is nonsingular.

Determine whether the following statement holds: for every choice of $f_1, f_2$ as above, the number of simple real solutions of the system $f_1=f_2=0$ in $(\mathbb{R}^*)^2$ is at most
$$ (2m_1 - 1)(2m_2 - 1), $$
and that this bound is attained for some choice of $f_1, f_2$ with prescribed values of $m_1, m_2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjectured sharp bound $(2m_1-1)(2m_2-1)$ for the number of nondegenerate real solutions of a bivariate fewnomial system is a long-standing modified Kouchnirenko-type conjecture. Sharp results are known only in special cases (e.g., Li–Rojas–Wang proved the bound 5 for two trinomials in the positive quadrant), and Bihan–Sottile and others have given partial results and lower bound constructions, but the general conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Counting Real Connected Components of Trinomial Curve Intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Any pair of bivariate trinomials has at most five isolated roots in the positive quadrant; this sharp bound improves earlier Khovanskii bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp bounds are known only in restricted cases (two trinomials), not in the general bivariate fewnomial setting.

status_evidence.title: On the sharpness of fewnomial bounds and the number of components of fewnomial hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses sharpness of fewnomial bounds for real solutions of polynomial systems.
status_evidence.claim: The general $(2m_1-1)(2m_2-1)$ bound for bivariate real fewnomial systems is studied as an open conjecture.
